picks.intervention_label: Active surveillance (no adjuvant systemic therapy); structured cross-sectional imaging q3-6 months for 2-3 years, then space out
picks.rationale: The adjuvant decision is the one place in this dossier where the high-quality evidence points somewhere, and it points away from drugs. The registration-grade adjuvant-imatinib RCTs (Z9001; SSGXVIII at 10 years; PERSIST-5; all RoB2 Low) enrolled KIT-driven disease and structurally excluded SDH-deficient GIST, and ESMO recommends against imatinib here because Boikos 2016 saw 1/49 (2%) responses in this subset. No RCT, and no single-arm trial, supports any adjuvant systemic therapy in dSDH-GIST. Recurrence is common (Mei 2018: ~71%, median EFS 2.5 yr) but the biology is indolent, so structured imaging beats committing an NED patient to chronic toxicity with zero supporting trial.
primary_concerns: Indirectness: the adjuvant RCTs that justify withholding treatment come from a KIT-mutant population, so the no-adjuvant call here is an absence-of-evidence inference rather than a trial-tested one.

The natural-history recurrence figures (Mei 2018) come from a narrative review citing a retrospective surgical cohort (tier 5, ROBINS-I not gradable); fine for framing surveillance intensity, not for hard risk quantitation.

picks.intervention_label: Confirm the molecular foundation: SDHB/SDHA IHC re-cut with internal control, SDHA germline-vs-somatic panel, tumor-tissue NGS confirmation of the ctDNA-only variants
picks.rationale: Before any molecular rationale earns a vote, the molecular calls have to hold. SDHB IHC reads intact while two somatic SDHA variants sit at roughly 85% combined VAF, and biallelic SDHA inactivation should collapse the complex and wipe out SDHB staining, so the discordance needs a re-cut with a positive internal control before the dSDH label is load-bearing. The PIK3CA R93W, MAP2K1 P124S, and SDHA E350fs calls are ctDNA-only and unconfirmed in tissue, and R93W sits outside the alpelisib/inavolisib companion-diagnostic hotspots. One tissue pull resolves the driver call, the germline-vs-somatic SDHA question, and the eligibility gate for every recurrence trial downstream.
primary_concerns: Measurement/classification risk: SDHB-IHC intact against biallelic SDHA is an internal contradiction; accepting the current stain risks misclassifying the driver.

ctDNA-only variant calls carry clonal-hematopoiesis and assay-artifact risk with no orthogonal tissue confirmation yet; R93W and P124S in particular should not gate any therapy until tissue confirms them.

picks.intervention_label: Sunitinib 50 mg PO 4-on/2-off (or 37.5 mg continuous) at first measurable recurrence; NOT adjuvant
picks.rationale: At measurable recurrence, sunitinib is the best-evidenced systemic option here, which is a low bar met rather than a strong endorsement. Its own pivotal is RCT-grade (Demetri 2006, n=312, TTP HR 0.33, p<0.0001, RoB2 Low) but did not stratify SDH status and was overwhelmingly KIT-mutant, so the subtype-specific claim rests on Boikos 2016: 7/38 (18%) SDH-deficient responders on sunitinib vs 1/49 (2%) on imatinib, retrospective and ROBINS-I Moderate. Read the 18% as directional, not as a dependable response estimate. It edges out regorafenib and ripretinib only because their dSDH evidence base is thinner still.
primary_concerns: Indirectness: the pivotal RCT population was KIT-mutant with no SDH stratification, so the HR 0.33 does not transport cleanly to this subtype.
Boikos 2016 is retrospective (ROBINS-I Moderate) with small per-drug n and no per-AE capture; selection and confounding risk sit inside the 18% response figure.

picks.intervention_label: Rogaratinib (pan-FGFR1-4 inhibitor) at recurrence, trial route only (NCI cohort closed; FGFR-pathway evidence anchor)
picks.rationale: Rogaratinib has the highest ORR reported for any systemic agent in this subtype, 10/24 (41.7%) PR with mPFS 31.0 mo (95% CI 20.2-NR), in the exact molecular population. That is a real signal worth a trial referral, but it comes from one single-arm, open-label phase 2 of n=24 with no comparator and an ORR endpoint, and per-term AE rates I cannot verify: the abstract names only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea, the CT.gov results tab is empty, and the full text is paywalled. The cohort enrolled regardless of FGFR status, so the response is not anchored to a predictive biomarker. It is unreplicated; the confirmatory pemigatinib trial (NCT07434843) has not read out, and rogaratinib's own cohort is closed to accrual.
primary_concerns: Single-arm open-label ORR endpoint: no comparator and unblinded response ascertainment, with a real risk that dSDH indolence inflates the 50% SD fraction in the 91.7% DCR.

Selective/incomplete outcome reporting: per-term AE data are not retrievable from abstract, CT.gov, or the paywalled full text, so the safety profile is unverified (I read the abstract and the structured row, not the full paper).
No replication; the FGFR rationale rests on the Flavahan FGF4-insulator mechanism, which is mechanistic plausibility rather than clinical confirmation.

picks.intervention_label: Olverembatinib (multikinase TKI) at recurrence, trial route only (phase 1b signal; phase-3 NCT06640361 watch)
picks.rationale: Olverembatinib shows 6/26 (23.1%, 95% CI 9-43.7) PR and mPFS 25.7 mo, but the design is a single-arm phase 1b expansion of n=26 inside a 66-patient basket, and the safety table is pooled across all 66 rather than the GIST cohort. The mechanism is non-canonical for a KIT/PDGFRA-WT tumor: this is a KIT/ABL TKI acting through VEGFR/FGFR/HIF-CD36 axes, not its labeled target, so plausibility is borrowed rather than demonstrated in-indication. The NCT06640361 'phase 3' is phase-3 in name only, being open-label, single intervention, no comparator arm, n=40, with a PFS-rate endpoint. That design will not deliver randomized evidence, and the SDHB-IHC-loss entry criterion is one this patient does not currently meet.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 1b with an ORR endpoint; safety pooled across the 66-patient basket rather than the n=26 GIST cohort, so subtype-specific tolerability is unresolved.
The confirmatory NCT06640361 is labeled phase 3 but is single-arm/no-comparator with a PFS-rate surrogate, so it will not generate RCT-grade evidence.
Non-canonical MoA in a KIT-WT tumor: the efficacy claim cannot lean on the labeled target.

picks.intervention_label: Temozolomide with MGMT-methylation enrichment, trial route only; late contingency at recurrence
picks.rationale: Temozolomide is a contingency, not a recommendation, and the evidence is thin enough that I would only run it on a trial with MGMT enrichment. The clinical anchor is Yebra 2022: 2/5 (40%) PR in SDH-mutant GIST, which is n=5, a translational case series, ROBINS-I Serious, tier 4, with no per-AE table. The one biomarker lever is real (Giger 2022: MGMT promoter hypermethylation in 8/33 (24%) SDH-deficient tumors and 0% elsewhere), so methylation testing could enrich for the likely responders before exposing anyone to an alkylator. A 5-patient series is hypothesis-generating; it does not support TMZ as a default off-label move.
primary_concerns: n=5 case series, ROBINS-I Serious, tier 4: severe small-sample and selection bias, with a 40% ORR whose confidence interval is wide enough to be uninformative.
No per-AE safety table in the source, so toxicity in this exact population is uncharacterized.
The MGMT-methylation predictive value (Giger 2022) is a retrospective biomarker association, not validated as a treatment-selection marker in a prospective trial.

notes: Not abstaining: for the adjuvant question the high-quality evidence is unusually clear and supports surveillance, so I have a confident rank 1 for once. Three mechanism-matched strategies are already closed by negative subtype-specific trials and I ranked none of them: guadecitabine 0/9 (Ligon 2023, terminated for accrual), linsitinib 0/20 (von Mehren 2020), vandetanib 0/9 (Glod 2019); their 'stable disease' fractions most plausibly reflect dSDH indolence rather than drug effect, which is also the main reason I discount the single-arm DCR figures for rogaratinib and olverembatinib. I deliberately ranked no PI3Kalpha (alpelisib/inavolisib/RLY-2608) or MEK (trametinib) option: R93W and P124S are ctDNA-only and non-canonical, the registration data are breast-cancer cross-tumor, and the trametinib MAP2K1 precedent is cross-tumor and cross-class. POLE R1679C with TMB<1 and MSS gives no ICI rationale; that is a genetic-counseling item, not a therapy. For rogaratinib and olverembatinib I read the abstracts plus the structured rows, not the full texts, so my AE-completeness criticisms are bounded by that.
